append_file.description: Append text to the end of a file, creating the file if it does not exist. The existing content is never changed or replaced. The text is appended exactly as given, with no newline added before or after it, so end it with a newline if the next append should start on a new line. Only works within allowed directories.

content.description: Text to append, exactly as given. No newline is added: end it with \n if the next append should start on a new line.

path.description: The file to append to; it is created if it does not exist. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

append_file.name: append_file
append_file.title: Append File

copy_file.description: Copy a file to a new location, without reading its content into the conversation. Copies one regular file, keeping its permissions and modification time; directories are not copied. If the destination exists, the operation will fail: it never overwrites. Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.

destination.description: Where to create the copy; nothing may exist there yet

copy_file.name: copy_file
copy_file.title: Copy File

create_directory.description: Create a new directory or ensure a directory exists. Can create multiple nested directories in one operation. If the directory already exists, this operation will succeed silently. Perfect for setting up directory structures for projects or ensuring required paths exist. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The directory to create, with any missing parents; an existing directory is left as is. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

create_directory.name: create_directory
create_directory.title: Create Directory

directory_tree.description: Get a recursive tree view of files and directories as a JSON structure. Each entry includes 'name', 'type' (file/directory), and 'children' for directories. Files have no children array, while directories always have a children array (which may be empty), except at the last level when 'depth' limits the tree: those directories are not read and have no children array. The output is formatted with 2-space indentation for readability. Only works within allowed directories.

depth.description: How many levels to descend: 1 lists only the entries directly in path. Directories at the last level have no children array. Omit for the whole tree.

excludePatterns.description: Patterns for entries to leave out, with their contents, matched against each entry's path relative to path. A pattern with no '*' matches that name at any depth ('node_modules' leaves out every node_modules directory); a pattern with '*' is a glob matched as written, and one ending in '/**' also leaves out the directory it names.

path.description: The directory at the root of the tree. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

directory_tree.name: directory_tree
directory_tree.title: Directory Tree

edit_file.description: Make line-based edits to a text file. Edits apply in order, each to the result of the ones before it, and each replaces the first match of its oldText with newText. oldText must match the file's text exactly, except that line endings (LF or CRLF) never matter and, when there is no exact match, a run of whole lines matches if each line is equal once leading and trailing whitespace is ignored (newText then takes the file's indentation). Whitespace inside a line must match. If any edit has no match, nothing is written and the error shows the closest lines of the file, numbered, to copy oldText from. Returns a git-style diff showing the changes made. Only works within allowed directories.

dryRun.description: Preview changes using git-style diff format

edits.description: The replacements to make, applied in order, each to the result of the ones before it. If any one has no match, none is written.

oldText.description: Text to search for - must match exactly

path.description: The text file to edit. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

edit_file.name: edit_file
edit_file.title: Edit File

get_file_info.description: Retrieve detailed metadata about a file or directory. Returns comprehensive information including size, creation time, last modified time, permissions, type and hard-link count. This tool is perfect for understanding file characteristics without reading the actual content. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The file or directory to describe. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

get_file_info.name: get_file_info
get_file_info.title: Get File Info

list_allowed_directories.description: Returns the list of directories that this server is allowed to access. Subdirectories within these allowed directories are also accessible. Use this to understand which directories and their nested paths are available before trying to access files.
list_allowed_directories.name: list_allowed_directories
list_allowed_directories.title: List Allowed Directories

list_directory.description: List the files and directories directly inside a path, each marked [FILE] or [DIR]. Use it to see what a directory contains; when you also need each entry's size or want entries sorted by size, use list_directory_with_sizes instead, and for a recursive view use directory_tree. Returns one line per entry. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The directory to list. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

list_directory.name: list_directory
list_directory.title: List Directory

list_directory_with_sizes.description: List the files and directories directly inside a path with each file's size, marked [FILE] or [DIR], sorted by name or by size, largest first (sortBy). Use it when sizes matter, such as finding the largest files; for names only, use list_directory, which returns less text. Returns one line per entry, followed by the totals. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The directory to list. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

sortBy.description: Sort entries by name or size

list_directory_with_sizes.name: list_directory_with_sizes
list_directory_with_sizes.title: List Directory with Sizes

move_file.description: Move or rename files and directories. Can move files between directories and rename them in a single operation. If the destination exists, the operation will fail. Works across different directories and can be used for simple renaming within the same directory. Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.

destination.description: Its new path, including the name; nothing may exist there yet. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

source.description: The file or directory to move or rename. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

move_file.name: move_file
move_file.title: Move File

read_file.description: Read the complete contents of a file as text. DEPRECATED: Use read_text_file instead.

head.description: If provided, returns only the first N lines of the file

path.description: The file to read as text. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

tail.description: If provided, returns only the last N lines of the file

read_file.name: read_file
read_file.title: Read File (Deprecated)

read_media_file.description: Read a file and return it as a base64-encoded content block with its MIME type. Image and audio files are returned as image/audio content; any other file type is returned as an embedded resource. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The image, audio or other file to read as base64. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

read_media_file.name: read_media_file
read_media_file.title: Read Media File

read_multiple_files.description: Read the contents of multiple files simultaneously. This is more efficient than reading files one by one when you need to analyze or compare multiple files. Each file's content is returned with its path as a reference. Failed reads for individual files won't stop the entire operation. Only works within allowed directories.

paths.description: Array of file paths to read. Each path must be a string pointing to a valid file within allowed directories.

read_multiple_files.name: read_multiple_files
read_multiple_files.title: Read Multiple Files

read_text_file.description: Read the complete contents of a file from the file system as text. Handles various text encodings and provides detailed error messages if the file cannot be read. Use this tool when you need to examine the contents of a single file. Use the 'head' parameter to read only the first N lines of a file, or the 'tail' parameter to read only the last N lines of a file. Operates on the file as text regardless of extension. Only works within allowed directories.

head.description: If provided, returns only the first N lines of the file

path.description: The file to read as text. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

tail.description: If provided, returns only the last N lines of the file

read_text_file.name: read_text_file
read_text_file.title: Read Text File

search_files.description: Find files and directories by NAME, not by content: this tool never reads or searches inside files. It walks the tree under 'path' and matches a glob pattern against each entry's path relative to 'path' (case-sensitive). Use '*.ext' to match entries directly under 'path', and '**/*.ext' or '**/name' to match at any depth. Returns full paths to all matching items. Great for finding files when you don't know their exact location. Only searches within allowed directories.

excludePatterns.description: Patterns for entries to leave out, with their contents, matched against each entry's path relative to path. A pattern with no '*' matches that name at any depth ('node_modules' leaves out every node_modules directory); a pattern with '*' is a glob matched as written, and one ending in '/**' also leaves out the directory it names.

path.description: The directory to search under. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

pattern.description: Glob matched against each entry's path relative to path, never its content: '*.ts' matches directly under path, '**/*.ts' at any depth.

search_files.name: search_files
search_files.title: Search Files

write_file.description: Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with new content. Use with caution as it will overwrite existing files without warning. Handles text content with proper encoding. Only works within allowed directories.

content.description: The complete text the file will contain, replacing any it had

path.description: The file to create, or to overwrite if it exists; its parent directory must exist. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

write_file.name: write_file
write_file.title: Write File

create_directory.description: Create a new directory or ensure a directory exists. Can create multiple nested directories in one operation. If the directory already exists, this operation will succeed silently. Perfect for setting up directory structures for projects or ensuring required paths exist. Only works within allowed directories.
create_directory.name: create_directory

directory_tree.description: Get a recursive tree view of files and directories as a JSON structure. Each entry includes 'name', 'type' (file/directory), and 'children' for directories. Files have no children array, while directories always have a children array (which may be empty). The output is formatted with 2-space indentation for readability. Only works within allowed directories.
directory_tree.name: directory_tree

edit_file.description: Make line-based edits to a text file. Each edit replaces exact line sequences with new content. Returns a git-style diff showing the changes made. Only works within allowed directories.
edit_file.name: edit_file

get_file_info.description: Retrieve detailed metadata about a file or directory. Returns comprehensive information including size, creation time, last modified time, permissions, and type. This tool is perfect for understanding file characteristics without reading the actual content. Only works within allowed directories.
get_file_info.name: get_file_info

list_allowed_directories.description: Returns the list of directories that this server is allowed to access. Subdirectories within these allowed directories are also accessible. Use this to understand which directories and their nested paths are available before trying to access files.
list_allowed_directories.name: list_allowed_directories

list_directory.description: Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path. Results clearly distinguish between files and directories with [FILE] and [DIR] prefixes. This tool is essential for understanding directory structure and finding specific files within a directory. Only works within allowed directories.
list_directory.name: list_directory

list_directory_with_sizes.description: Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path, including sizes. Results clearly distinguish between files and directories with [FILE] and [DIR] prefixes. This tool is useful for understanding directory structure and finding specific files within a directory. Only works within allowed directories.
list_directory_with_sizes.name: list_directory_with_sizes

move_file.description: Move or rename files and directories. Can move files between directories and rename them in a single operation. If the destination exists, the operation will fail. Works across different directories and can be used for simple renaming within the same directory. Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.
move_file.name: move_file

read_file.description: Read the complete contents of a file as text. DEPRECATED: Use read_text_file instead.
read_file.name: read_file

read_media_file.description: Read an image or audio file. Returns the base64 encoded data and MIME type. Only works within allowed directories.
read_media_file.name: read_media_file

read_multiple_files.description: Read the contents of multiple files simultaneously. This is more efficient than reading files one by one when you need to analyze or compare multiple files. Each file's content is returned with its path as a reference. Failed reads for individual files won't stop the entire operation. Only works within allowed directories.
read_multiple_files.name: read_multiple_files

read_text_file.description: Read the complete contents of a file from the file system as text. Handles various text encodings and provides detailed error messages if the file cannot be read. Use this tool when you need to examine the contents of a single file. Use the 'head' parameter to read only the first N lines of a file, or the 'tail' parameter to read only the last N lines of a file. Operates on the file as text regardless of extension. Only works within allowed directories.
read_text_file.name: read_text_file

search_files.description: Recursively search for files and directories matching a pattern. Searches through all subdirectories from the starting path. The search is case-insensitive and matches partial names. Returns full paths to all matching items. Great for finding files when you don't know their exact location. Only searches within allowed directories.
search_files.name: search_files

write_file.description: Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with new content. Use with caution as it will overwrite existing files without warning. Handles text content with proper encoding. Only works within allowed directories.
write_file.name: write_file

add_observations.description: Add new observations to existing entities in the knowledge graph

observations.description: The observations to add, grouped by entity. Each entity must already exist; an observation it already has is not added again

contents.description: An array of observation contents to add

entityName.description: The name of the entity to add the observations to

add_observations.name: add_observations
add_observations.title: Add Observations

create_entities.description: Create multiple new entities in the knowledge graph. An entity whose name already exists, or repeats an earlier entity in the same call, is skipped and its observations are not added; the result lists the skipped names in `skipped`. Use add_observations to add observations to an existing entity.

entities.description: The entities to create, each with a name unique in the graph

observations.description: An array of observation contents associated with the entity

create_entities.name: create_entities

observations.description: An array of observation contents associated with the entity

create_entities.title: Create Entities

create_relations.description: Create multiple new relations between entities in the knowledge graph. Relations should be in active voice

relations.description: The relations to create. Both ends must name existing entities; a relation already in the graph is not added again

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

create_relations.name: create_relations

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

create_relations.title: Create Relations

delete_entities.description: Delete whole entities from the knowledge graph, together with every relation that points to or from them and all their observations. Use it only to remove an entity entirely; to remove a link between two entities and keep both, use delete_relations, and to remove facts from an entity, use delete_observations. Cannot be undone.

entityNames.description: An array of entity names to delete

delete_entities.name: delete_entities
delete_entities.title: Delete Entities

delete_observations.description: Delete specific observations from entities in the knowledge graph

deletions.description: The observations to delete, grouped by entity, each matched by its exact text

entityName.description: The name of the entity containing the observations

observations.description: An array of observations to delete

delete_observations.name: delete_observations
delete_observations.title: Delete Observations

delete_relations.description: Delete specific relations (from, to, relationType) from the knowledge graph and keep the entities they connect. Each relation must match an existing one exactly on all three fields; if unsure, call open_nodes (or search_nodes) first to read the stored relationType. Use it to remove a link between two entities; to remove an entity itself, use delete_entities. Cannot be undone.

relations.description: An array of relations to delete

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

delete_relations.name: delete_relations
delete_relations.title: Delete Relations

open_nodes.description: Retrieve specific entities by their exact names, with every relation that touches one of them. Use this when you already know the names (from the conversation, or from an earlier search_nodes or read_graph result); it is the cheapest way to read entities you can name. Prefer search_nodes when you only have a keyword or part of a name. Names that do not exist are skipped.

names.description: An array of entity names to retrieve

observationLimit.description: Return at most this many observations per entity (the first ones, in the order they were added) and add each entity's total as observationCount. Use 0 for names, types and counts only: a cheap overview of a large graph, after which open_nodes reads the entities you need in full. Omit to return every observation.

open_nodes.name: open_nodes

observationCount.description: How many observations the entity holds in total; present only when observationLimit was given

observations.description: An array of observation contents associated with the entity

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

open_nodes.title: Open Nodes

read_graph.description: Read the entire knowledge graph: every entity with its observations, and every relation. The result grows with the graph, so use this only when you need everything; prefer search_nodes to find entities by keyword and open_nodes to read entities whose names you know.

entityTypes.description: Return only entities whose entityType is one of these (exact match), and only the relations that touch one of them. Omit to return every entity.

observationLimit.description: Return at most this many observations per entity (the first ones, in the order they were added) and add each entity's total as observationCount. Use 0 for names, types and counts only: a cheap overview of a large graph, after which open_nodes reads the entities you need in full. Omit to return every observation.

read_graph.name: read_graph

observationCount.description: How many observations the entity holds in total; present only when observationLimit was given

observations.description: An array of observation contents associated with the entity

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

read_graph.title: Read Graph

search_nodes.description: Search the knowledge graph for entities whose name, type or observations contain the query (case-insensitive). Use this when you have a keyword, a topic or part of a name but not the exact entity names. Prefer open_nodes when you already know the exact names, and use read_graph only when you need the whole graph. Returns the matching entities and every relation that touches one of them.

limit.description: Return at most this many matching entities (the first matches, in stored order), with the relations that touch them. Omit to return every match.

observationLimit.description: Return at most this many observations per entity (the first ones, in the order they were added) and add each entity's total as observationCount. Use 0 for names, types and counts only: a cheap overview of a large graph, after which open_nodes reads the entities you need in full. Omit to return every observation.

query.description: The search query to match against entity names, types, and observation content

search_nodes.name: search_nodes

observationCount.description: How many observations the entity holds in total; present only when observationLimit was given

observations.description: An array of observation contents associated with the entity

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

search_nodes.title: Search Nodes
